น่าน.title: US interest rates raised for first time in three years
น่าน.summary:
US interest rates have been raised for the first time in more than three years and could be increased further in a bid to slow rising prices.

Rates were hiked to 3.75%-4% from 3.5%-3.75% by the Federal Reserve in a unanimous decision, despite fierce opposition from President Donald Trump, who had called for rates to be cut.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the move was because "inflation is too high and has been for too long", adding that it was a "sober" and "responsible decision".

After the announcement, Trump expressed support for Warsh but said the Fed board, which votes on rate decisions, was "hostile".

Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive for people wanting to secure loans, mortgages, and credit cards, but can lead to better returns on savings.

Warsh said during a press conference on Wednesday following the decision that, while there was "an attitude of optimism" within the Fed leadership, inflation remained a problem.

Like many central banks, the Fed has a target of keeping inflation at 2% or below. Warsh noted that US inflation has been above the target "for more than five years".

That has helped make affordability one of the top concerns of American voters, who have seen fuel prices surge in response to soaring wholesale oil prices since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran. This has driven up the cost of many goods and services, as well.

While the Fed "cannot affect any individual price â whether it be oil prices, whether it be food stuffs at the grocery store", Warsh said, the central bank can work to keep price rises from broadening across the economy.

He added that strength in the jobs market and wider economy meant the Fed was staying focused on stabilising prices, and that those least well off had the most to gain from lower inflation.

Central banks tend to increase rates when inflation is high to discourage spending and encourage saving, in the hope this will reduce the pace of price rises. But it's a balancing act, as higher rates can also encourage businesses to hold off on investing and hurt economic growth.

When he was confirmed, Democratic lawmakers had said Warsh would be Trump's "sock puppet" and many Fed watchers expected him to carry out Trump's persistent demands to slash rates. Trump had been heavily critical of Warsh's predecessor Jerome Powell for not cutting them.

Asked on Wednesday about the message the rate hike sent to Trump, Warsh chuckled before saying: "I have got nothing for you on a discussion with the president."

Trump told reporters later "I'm relying on Kevin [Warsh], but he's got, you know, a very tough board".

"And the, interest rates are too high. They're not appropriate... I talked to Kevin and I said, 'you might as well vote with the board because it's not going to matter.' The board is very hostile, they're very political," he added.

Earlier, Trump said on social media: "LOWER THE INTEREST RATES FOR THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, AND FAST!"

Democrats on Capitol Hill said the rate increase would make loans costlier and, in turn, more Americans would go into debt.

"This is going to make everything become more expensive," said Chuck Schumer, the top Democrat in the Senate. "This is because Donald Trump does not know how to manage the economy."

The Fed's hike is the first rate move in any direction since they were cut in December 2025. The last time they were raised was in July 2023.

น่าน.title: Commentary: Asia has to prepare before climate disasters, not just cope after they strike
น่าน.summary:
When it comes to climate adaptation and resilience in the region, there are wide gaps between estimated needs and available capacity and finance, says former foreign correspondent Nirmal Ghosh.

SINGAPORE: The devastation from recent catastrophes across Asia has been shocking: The collapse of a glacier in Nepal unleashed a monster flood in August with a death toll that is still rising; Indonesia is battling its worst wildfires in years on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra, which shrouded the region in smoke.

But the broader climate picture is less surprising. The world is on the brink of exceeding a 1.5°C rise in average temperature above pre-industrial levels. This year’s El Nino, the phenomenon associated with dry and hot extremes, is set to be the most intense on record.

Asia is warming nearly twice as fast as the global average. Southeast Asia in particular is one of the world’s most disaster-prone regions, with intensifying events driven by warmer temperatures, threatening food security.

Yet the region remains largely underequipped to deal with the consequences of global warming.

There are wide gaps between estimated needs and available capacity and finance, when it comes to climate adaptation and resilience. Put simply, adaptation is about taking measures to avoid or moderate damage from climate and weather-driven events, while resilience is about coping with and recovering from them.

An assessment published in May by Singapore’s Temasek Trust concluded that by 2030, Asia will account for around 75 per cent of the global climate adaptation and resilience financing gap. “More than US$200 billion is required annually across the region, yet current flows stand at only around US$19 billion,” it said.

A paper by McKinsey, also in May, zeroed in on Southeast Asia. It concluded that to protect the region today to the adaptation standards of developed economies, it would need additional investment of about US$25 billion per year, bringing total annual investment to US$37 billion.

This gap has consequences that are being lived with now, in the thousands displaced by the Nepal disaster, the human health costs of bad air quality in lower Southeast Asia, and the looming agriculture crisis.

While poorer people bear the brunt, the wealthy are not exempt; Asian companies are projected to bear around US$336 billion in annual climate costs, the Temasek study concluded.

Additionally, Singapore-based OCBC Group Research in a Sep 9 bulletin warned that it sees India, the Philippines, Thailand and Indonesia as economies with high exposure to the effects of El Nino. Malaysia and Vietnam face “meaningful but more concentrated risks”.

"The main impact will be higher food prices, with rice, wheat, maize and vegetable oils most exposed," wrote OCBC.

But closing that gap requires not just money. Prioritising adaptation and resilience would require a fundamental shift from reacting after disasters happen to proactively investing in prevention – which means hard decisions.

In the case of Nepal, the death toll and destruction may have geological and climate triggers but it was high because of poor planning, governance failure, and lack of enforcement of zoning laws that allowed building settlements and infrastructure along floodplains, Kunda Dixit, Kathmandu-based publisher, author and lecturer on climate change told me.

น่าน.title: ซาอุดีอาระเบีย-ฮูตีแลกหมัดโจมตีเดือด ชาวเยเมนลงเรือออกทะเลแดง ลี้ภัยสงคราม
น่าน.summary:
ซาอุดีอาระเบีย-ฮูตีแลกหมัดโจมตีเดือด ชาวเยเมนลงเรือออกทะเลแดง ลี้ภัยสงคราม
เมื่อวันที่ 17 กันยายน ซาอุดีอาระเบียและกลุ่มฮูตี ซึ่งได้รับการสนับสนุนจากอิหร่านในเยเมน เปิดฉากโจมตีตอบโต้กันระลอกใหม่ โดยซาอุดีอาระเบียได้เปิดฉากโจมตีทางอากาศพื้นที่ชายแดนในจังหวัดฮัจญะห์ รวมถึงพื้นที่โดยรอบเมืองตาอิซ ซึ่งอยู่ลึกเข้าไปทางตอนใต้ของประเทศ โดยหน่วยงานป้องกันภัยฝ่ายพลเรือนของซาอุดีอาระเบียเปิดเผยว่า ชาวเยเมนที่อาศัยอยู่ในซาอุดีอาระเบียเสียชีวิตจากเศษซากโดรน ซึ่งร่วงหล่นลงมาจากการสกัดกั้นในทางตอนเหนือของเมืองตาอิซ นับเป็นผู้เสียชีวิตรายแรกที่ทางการซาอุดีอาระเบียประกาศยืนยัน นับตั้งแต่กลุ่มฮูตีดำเนินการโจมตีหลายครั้ง หลังก่อนหน้านี้ ซาอุดีอาระเบียระบุว่า มีผู้ได้รับบาดเจ็บแล้วกว่า 80 คน
กลุ่มฮูตีกล่าวว่า กองทัพอากาศซาอุดีอาระเบียได้ปฏิบัติการโจมตีทางอากาศหลายร้อยครั้งในช่วงไม่กี่วันที่ผ่านมา ทั้งนี้ เมื่อวันพุธ (16 ก.ย.) ทางกลุ่มสามารถยิงเครื่องบินขับไล่ F-15 ของซาอุดีอาระเบียตกได้ ขณะที่อับดุล มาลิก อัล-ฮูตี ผู้นำกลุ่มฮูตี กล่าวว่า ต้องการให้ซาอุดีอาระเบียยุติการปิดล้อม ยึดครองประเทศและยุติการรุกรานต่อเรา ขณะที่มีมีดสั้นแบบดั้งเดิมคาดอยู่ที่เอว และบนผนังด้านหลังมีข้อความว่า ความตายจงมีแด่อเมริกา ความตายจงมีแด่อิสราเอล คำสาปจงมีแด่ชาวยิว ชัยชนะจงมีแด่อิสลาม
ขณะเดียวกัน ชาวเยเมนจำนวนหนึ่งได้อพยพข้ามช่องแคบแคบบับ เอล-มันเดบ ซึ่งในภาษาอาหรับหมายถึง ประตูแห่งน้ำตา ด้วยเรือออกจากพื้นที่โจมตีในทะเลแดง โดยในบทสัมภาษณ์ขององค์การระหว่างประเทศเพื่อการโยกย้ายถิ่นฐาน (IOM) วาฮิดา โอเมอร์ วัย 50 ปี กล่าวที่จิบูตี บริเวณชายฝั่งแอฟริกาของทะเลแดง หลังจากที่เดินทางถึงฝั่งหลังโดยสารเรือขนาดเล็กข้ามจากเยเมน เนื่องจากหมู่บ้านดูบับของเธอถูกกลุ่มฮูตีโจมตีและยึดพื้นที่ ว่าทะเลน่ากลัวและข้ามมาได้ยากมาก ผู้ที่อยู่บนเรือร้องไห้ตลอดทาง และเมื่อมาถึงก็ยังร้องไห้ทั้งยังไม่มีอาหารรับประทาน พร้อมเผยว่าสามีของเธอยังอยู่ที่เยเมน และเธอไม่ทราบว่าเขายังมีชีวิตอยู่ เสียชีวิตหรือถูกกลุ่มฮูตีจับตัวไป
IOM ระบุด้วยว่า การสู้รบระลอกล่าสุดทำให้ชาวเยเมนต้องพลัดถิ่นมากกว่า 100,000 คน โดยส่วนใหญ่ยังคงอพยพอยู่ภายในประเทศ
การขยายตัวของสงครามอิหร่านเข้าสู่เยเมนและซาอุดีอาระเบียทำให้เกิดความกังวลครั้งใหม่เกี่ยวกับอุปทานน้ำมัน เนื่องจากพื้นที่ทะเลแดง ซึ่งเป็นเส้นทางหลักทางเลือกสำหรับการส่งออกน้ำมันจากภูมิภาคอ่าว ได้รับผลกระทบ ขณะที่การเดินเรือผ่านช่องแคบฮอร์มุซยังคงเผชิญข้อจำกัด
ด้านประธานาธิบดีโดนัลด์ ทรัมป์ ของสหรัฐ ได้ปฏิเสธคำร้องขอความช่วยเหลือทางทหารจากซาอุดีอาระเบียในการรับมือกับการโจมตีจากกลุ่มฮูตี ซึ่งเคยบรรลุการหยุดยิงกับสหรัฐเมื่อปี 2025 หลังจากสหรัฐเปิดฉากโจมตีกลุ่มฮูตีเป็นเวลานาน 2 เดือน และกล่าวว่า ใกล้ถึงเวลาที่จะตัดสินใจแล้วว่าจะกลับมาโจมตีอิหร่านครั้งใหญ่ โดยทำลายให้สิ้นซากหรือไม่
อีกทั้งทรัมป์กำลังเผชิญกับเสี่ยงของพรรครีพับลิกันในการสูญเสียที่นั่งในการเลือกตั้งกลางเทอมที่จะเกิดขึ้ดในเดือนพฤศจิกายนที่จะถึงนี้ โดยส่วนหนึ่งเป็นผลจากราคาพลังงานที่ปรับตัวสูงขึ้น นับตั้งแต่สหรัฐและอิสราเอลเปิดฉากโจมตีอิหร่านในเดือนกุมภาพันธ์
ในวันเดียวกันนี้ ราคาน้ำมันดิบของตลาดโลกปรับตัวลงเล็กน้อย แต่ยังคงอยู่เหนือระดับ 100 ดอลลาร์ต่อบาร์เรล หลังพุ่งแตะระดับสูงสุดนับตั้งแต่เดือนพฤษภาคม ส่วนราคาขายปลีกน้ำมันดีเซลโดยเฉลี่ยในสหรัฐทำสถิติสูงสุดเป็นประวัติการณ์ โดยอยู่ที่เกือบ 6.40 ดอลลาร์ต่อแกลลอน
สหรัฐและอิหร่านยังไม่มีกำหนดการเจรจาเพื่อยุติสงคราม นับตั้งแต่ข้อตกลงชั่วคราวที่บรรลุในเดือนมิถุนายนล่มลงภายในเวลาไม่กี่สัปดาห์ อย่างไรก็ตาม ประเด็นสงครามดังกล่าวจะถูกหยิบยกขึ้นหารือในการประชุมสมัชชาใหญ่แห่งสหประชาชาติในสัปดาห์หน้า ขณะเดียวกัน กระทรวงต่างประเทศสหรัฐเปิดเผยว่า คณะผู้แทนอิหร่านจะสามารถเข้าร่วมการประชุมได้
ทั้งนี้ ล่าสุดกองทัพเรือกองกำลังพิทักษ์การปฏิวัติอิหร่าน (IRGC) ระบุว่า เรือบรรทุกน้ำมันที่ชักธงประเทศโตโกเกิดไฟไหม้และหยุดการเดินเรือ หลังถูกโจมตีขณะพยายามแล่นผ่านช่องแคบฮอร์มุซ ซึ่งถือเป็นการผ่าน…

น่าน.title: Malaysia’s king allows former leader Najib to serve rest of his graft sentence under house arrest
น่าน.summary:
KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia (AP) — Malaysia’s king on Friday granted jailed former Prime Minister Najib Razak a rare royal clemency, allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison term for graft under house arrest.
The decision came at a suddenly convened Pardons Board meeting, a week after the board deferred Najib’s latest clemency application to a future meeting. It marked an unprecedented use of house arrest as a form of royal clemency in Malaysia and could renew debate over royal powers, the rule of law and the treatment of Malaysia’s most prominent corruption convict.
A statement issued by the Legal Affairs Department under the Prime Minister’s office said Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar has granted a “conditional pardon” for Najib during a Pardons Board meeting. Najib will be allowed to serve the remainder of his prison term under house arrest until Aug. 23, 2028, if he pays the 50 million ringgit fine ($12 million) imposed by the court, it said.
The statement said Najib must also follow conditions set, failing which the pardon will be forfeited. No details were provided.
Najib, 73, has been imprisoned since August 2022 after Malaysia’s top court upheld his conviction in a graft case linked to the multi-billion dollar looting of the state investment fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad.
He was originally sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined 210 million ringgit ($51.5 million) in 2020 for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving 42 million ringgit ($10.3 million) channeled into his bank accounts from SRC International, a former unit of 1MDB.
In January 2024, a Pardons Board chaired by the then-king halved his sentence to six years and reduced his fine to 50 million ringgit.
Najib has maintained the previous king, Sultan Abdullah Ahmad Shah, also issued an addendum order allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. But the High Court ruled that the alleged house arrest order was not enforceable because it had not been raised or discussed by the Pardons Board at its January 2024 meeting.
The house-arrest order also raises questions about a separate graft sentence for Najib.
In December 2025, Najib was found guilty for abuse of power and money laundering related to over $700 million channeled into his bank accounts from 1MDB, in his main trial tied to the fund. He was sentenced to another 15 years in prison and fined 11.4 billion ringgit ($2.8 billion), which is to take effect after his existing sentence ends. He is appealing that conviction.
House arrest had been discussed as part of broader criminal-justice reforms in Malaysia. In 2024, the government said proposed legislation allowing home detention in certain circumstances was aimed at reducing prison overcrowding and recidivism, not designed specifically for Najib.
Najib set up the 1MDB development fund shortly after he took office in 2009. Investigators allege at least $4.5 billion was stolen from the fund and laundered by Najib’s associates through layers of bank accounts in the U.S. and other countries. The funds were allegedly used to finance Hollywood films and extravagant purchases that included hotels, a luxury yacht, art and jewelry.
A national outrage over the 1MDB scandal led to the historic 2018 election defeat of the party that had governed Malaysia since independence from Britain in 1957.

น่าน.title: Indonesia welcomes its first aircraft carrier, prompting debate over cost and military ambitions
น่าน.summary:
JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Indonesia welcomed its first aircraft carrier Friday, a former Italian warship that the government says will strengthen the archipelago nation’s maritime security and disaster response capabilities.
The 41-year-old former ITS Giuseppe Garibaldi, with capacity for short takeoff and vertical landing aircraft and helicopters, was welcomed with a military ceremony upon its arrival at a naval base in North Jakarta’s Tanjung Priok seaport.
Italy in March agreed to give the carrier, which was retired in 2024, to Indonesia in a move aimed at boosting Italy’s broader defense engagement with the Southeast Asian country. Italy is seeking deals on submarines and aircraft, and gifting the carrier to Indonesia also saves it the cost of decommissioning the ship.
“We intend to use the ship primarily for military operations other than war, although it can also be deployed for combat missions if necessary,” Indonesian Navy chief Adm. Muhammad Ali told reporters after the ceremony. He said the carrier could serve the navy for another 15 to 20 years and could accommodate 14 helicopters or more, depending on their size.
Indonesia will become the second country in Southeast Asia with an aircraft carrier. Thailand’s HTMS Chakri Naruebet was commissioned in 1997 after being procured from Spain along with carrier-capable AV-8S Matador jump jets.
Ali said the carrier will be commissioned into the navy next week as the KRI Sriwijaya, honoring the Srivijaya empire, a maritime kingdom based in Sumatra that became one of Southeast Asia’s dominant naval and trading powers between the seventh and 13th centuries. Previously, the navy would name the carrier as KRI Gajah Mada.
Defense development was one of the top priorities for President Prabowo Subianto’s administration, as he has advocated an expansion of the military through the purchase of submarines, frigates, fighter jets , and missiles and pushed for more defense cooperation with various countries.
Indonesian Navy personnel and crew members stand aboard the Giuseppe Garibaldi, a former Italian Navy aircraft carrier, after its arrival at Tanjung Priok port in Jakarta, Indonesia, Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Tatan Syuflana)
But the Garibaldi acquisition has raised questions about whether Indonesia needs an aircraft carrier at all and whether the government should be spending millions of dollars to refurbish and operate an aging warship.
Indonesia’s Finance Ministry approved $450 million in financing for the aircraft carrier program in 2025. However, some lawmakers have warned the overall bill could be far higher. TB Hasanuddin, a member of Parliament’s Commission I, said the cost of retrofitting the carrier alone could reach 16 trillion rupiah (about $900 million).
Indonesia to convert the Garibaldi for handling disasters
Unlike major naval powers that use aircraft carriers to launch fighter jets far from home shores, Indonesia views the vessel as a mobile command center and support hub for helicopters, uncrewed aircraft and maritime operations across its thousands of islands.
Speaking during a disaster management meeting early this month, Prabowo said the vessel would help authorities combat forest and peatland fires that regularly blanket parts of Southeast Asia with hazardous haze.
“We will refurbish it and convert it into a carrier for helicopters and drones,” Prabowo said in a video briefing. “This will greatly help our disaster response.”

น่าน.title: Heavy rain and floods in northern Vietnam submerge homes and disrupt economy
น่าน.summary:
HANOI, Vietnam (AP) — Heavy rain caused flooding across parts of northern Vietnam on Thursday, disrupting travel, inundating homes and pushing several rivers above dangerous levels, authorities and state media said.
Rain has fallen across northern and north-central Vietnam this week, with some areas receiving more than 50 centimeters (19.7 inches), according to the disaster prevention department.
More than 2,000 homes have been submerged, many key transportation routes blocked and more than 1,000 households isolated. Ninh Binh and Thanh Hoa provinces, which include lowland and hilly areas south of the capital Hanoi, have been among the hardest hit.
Vietnam is among the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries and prone to flooding. A series of severe storms last year spurred the country to find new ways to prepare for and manage floods .
Local residents commute by boat through a flooded village on the outskirts of Hanoi, Vietnam Thursday, Sep. 17, 2026. (Pham Tuan Anh/VNA via AP)
In Thanh Hoa province, authorities told students to stay home because flooding had made travel to school dangerous, state media said.
Heavy rains and flooding have submerged or damaged about 10,014 hectares (24,745 acres) of rice and other crops, with the largest losses reported in Ninh Binh, Thanh Hoa and Nghe An provinces. Thousands of livestock and poultry also have been killed.
“The flood happens every year,” Ninh Binh resident Tran Ngoc Tai told national broadcaster VTV, adding that people were prepared with fresh water and food.
Many streets in Hanoi were deeply flooded Thursday morning, with water nearly a meter (3.2 feet) deep in some places, disrupting traffic and making it difficult for residents to get to work, take children to school or leave their homes.
Rainfall from Wednesday night to Thursday morning exceeded 15 centimeters (5.9 inches) in some areas, state media said.
Many high schools and universities in Hanoi remained closed or switched to online classes Thursday afternoon as heavy rain caused widespread flooding.
The rising waters of Bui River in the southwest outskirts of Hanoi threatened to flood homes, prompting authorities to deploy hundreds of soldiers to help residents move belongings to higher ground, state media said.
Local residents commute by boat through a flooded village on the outskirts of Hanoi, Vietnam Thursday, Sep. 17, 2026. (Nhat Anh/VNA via AP)
A cold air mass moving south is expected to bring five days of heavy rain to southern Vietnam including flood-prone Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam’s financial capital, starting Sept. 17, according to the Southern Regional Hydro-Meteorological Center.
Forecasters predict widespread rain through Sept. 21. Authorities have warned of flooding in low-lying areas and along waterways. Ho Chi Minh City is forecast to receive 10 to 20 centimeters (4 to 8 inches) of rain, with some areas getting more.
Vietnam experienced repeated severe flooding in 2025. Tropical Storm Wipha brought heavy rain and flooding in July, followed by more flooding and landslides in August when Tropical Storm Kajiki struck. Typhoon Bualoi killed at least 26 in September. In October, the historic cities of Hue and Hoi An in central Vietnam flooded, along with much of northern Vietnam .

น่าน.title: AirAsia's Fernandes says travel demand remains strong, current crisis 'far' less severe than Covid
น่าน.summary:
HONG KONG - AirAsia co-founder Tony Fernandes said on Friday that the low-cost carrier's challenges from soaring jet fuel costs were "far, far" less severe than those it faced during the Covid-19 pandemic, as he ​sought to reassure investors about ⁠the airline's financial health.

Speaking at a media briefing, Fernandes also said AirAsia had "strong liquidity" and was adept at managing cash, adding the current crisis was largely driven by geopolitical tensions and higher fuel prices, ‌while travel demand remained strong.

The briefing came two days after Reuters reported, citing sources, that Malaysia's government had asked Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air whether they could absorb AirAsia's domestic market share.

The sources said it was part of what ⁠they described as scenario planning while authorities monitor the financial health of Southeast Asia's largest low-cost carrier.

AirAsia's current liabilities stood at 18.4 billion ringgit ($4.52 billion) as of June 30, against cash and bank balances of 954 million ringgit.

Fernandes told reporters the second quarter marked the toughest period for the airline that controls about 60% of Malaysia's domestic ​market and he forecast improving conditions as AirAsia adjusts fares to reflect higher fuel costs.

The airline has been hit by soaring jet fuel costs stemming from the US-Israeli war ​on ‌Iran that surged 66% in the second quarter from the prior quarter to an average of $183 a barrel.

AirAsia shares closed 21% lower on Thursday after the Reuters report. ​Malaysian ⁠financial markets were closed on Wednesday for a public holiday.

AirAsia shares were trading 2% lower on Friday after falling as much as 5% earlier. The stock ⁠has lost more than 70% of its value so far this year.

AirAsia's large market share in Malaysia has made its financial challenges a significant concern for the government, sources previously told Reuters.

Fernandes said "no one can replace" AirAsia's 100 ⁠planes in the country overnight.

The group's load factor, which measures how well an ​airline is filling available seats, stood at 80% in the third quarter and it sees strong bookings for the fourth quarter, Fernandes said, adding he was optimistic about operations in Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand.

AirAsia reported a net loss of 831 million ‌ringgit for the second quarter ended ⁠June 30, hit by rising jet fuel ​costs and heavy foreign-exchange losses of 331 million ringgit.

น่าน.title: US Fed Rate Hike Rocks Thailand: Baht Drops and Gold Slips
น่าน.summary:
BANGKOK – The US Federal Reserve recently raised interest rates to fight off stubbornly high inflation across America. This major financial move sends strong economic ripples across the globe, and Thailand is definitely feeling the impact.

For Thai citizens and local businesses, the effects of this policy change are now showing up in daily life. From the neighborhood grocery store to the city gold shop, everyone is watching the market closely.

When the Fed increases rates, the US dollar usually becomes stronger and more attractive to global investors. As a direct result, the Thai Baht has weakened against the dollar, recently trading near 33.40. A weaker Baht makes imported goods more expensive for Thai shoppers, but it also brings some hidden economic benefits. Understanding how this balance works is vital for anyone living, working, or doing business in Thailand right now.

A weaker Baht is not entirely bad news for the country or its hard-working local residents. It actually provides a very helpful boost to Thailand’s massive export and tourism industries. When the Baht drops in value, Thai manufactured products become much cheaper for foreign buyers to purchase. Similarly, foreign tourists find that their home currency stretches much further when visiting beautiful Thai beaches and bustling cities.

However, the clear downside is that it costs much more to bring foreign goods into the country. Everything from imported energy fuels to foreign electronics will likely see a noticeable price bump very soon. This dynamic forces local businesses to carefully balance their operational costs to avoid hurting everyday consumers. The central bank continues to monitor these complex changes closely to keep the local economy running smoothly.

So far, Thai monetary policy remains highly accommodating to strongly support ongoing business growth and national recovery. Financial leaders genuinely believe that the weaker currency is largely positive, as long as it avoids extreme volatility. Officials want to ensure that the economic recovery stays firmly on track without causing sudden global supply chain shocks. This careful and measured approach helps maintain public confidence during a time of global financial uncertainty.

The recent interest rate hike also sent massive economic shockwaves through the global gold market this week. Generally, when US interest rates go up, gold becomes far less appealing to large international investors. This happens because gold does not pay any regular interest, unlike standard savings accounts or government bonds. Consequently, the global spot price for gold took a noticeable plunge immediately following the Fed’s official announcement.

Here in Thailand, local gold buyers saw a very sharp and sudden drop in retail prices today. The domestic price for Thai gold dropped by roughly 500 Baht per Baht-weight almost overnight. However, the weakened local currency actually helped soften the harsh blow of the global price crash. น่าน.title_original: US Fed Rate Hike Rocks Thailand: Baht Drops and Gold Slips
น่าน.summary_original:
BANGKOK – The US Federal Reserve recently raised interest rates to fight off stubbornly high inflation across America. This major financial move sends strong economic ripples across the globe, and Thailand is definitely feeling the impact.

For Thai citizens and local businesses, the effects of this policy change are now showing up in daily life. From the neighborhood grocery store to the city gold shop, everyone is watching the market closely.

When the Fed increases rates, the US dollar usually becomes stronger and more attractive to global investors. As a direct result, the Thai Baht has weakened against the dollar, recently trading near 33.40. A weaker Baht makes imported goods more expensive for Thai shoppers, but it also brings some hidden economic benefits. Understanding how this balance works is vital for anyone living, working, or doing business in Thailand right now.

A weaker Baht is not entirely bad news for the country or its hard-working local residents. It actually provides a very helpful boost to Thailand’s massive export and tourism industries. When the Baht drops in value, Thai manufactured products become much cheaper for foreign buyers to purchase. Similarly, foreign tourists find that their home currency stretches much further when visiting beautiful Thai beaches and bustling cities.

However, the clear downside is that it costs much more to bring foreign goods into the country. Everything from imported energy fuels to foreign electronics will likely see a noticeable price bump very soon. This dynamic forces local businesses to carefully balance their operational costs to avoid hurting everyday consumers. The central bank continues to monitor these complex changes closely to keep the local economy running smoothly.

So far, Thai monetary policy remains highly accommodating to strongly support ongoing business growth and national recovery. Financial leaders genuinely believe that the weaker currency is largely positive, as long as it avoids extreme volatility. Officials want to ensure that the economic recovery stays firmly on track without causing sudden global supply chain shocks. This careful and measured approach helps maintain public confidence during a time of global financial uncertainty.

The recent interest rate hike also sent massive economic shockwaves through the global gold market this week. Generally, when US interest rates go up, gold becomes far less appealing to large international investors. This happens because gold does not pay any regular interest, unlike standard savings accounts or government bonds. Consequently, the global spot price for gold took a noticeable plunge immediately following the Fed’s official announcement.

Here in Thailand, local gold buyers saw a very sharp and sudden drop in retail prices today. The domestic price for Thai gold dropped by roughly 500 Baht per Baht-weight almost overnight. However, the weakened local currency actually helped soften the harsh blow of the global price crash. If the Thai Baht had remained strong, the local price drop would have been far more severe for investors.

น่าน.title: SK Hynix's Solidigm unit is weighing NAND memory chip factory in US, sources say
น่าน.summary:
SEOUL, Sept 18 : Chipmaker SK Hynix's US subsidiary Solidigm is considering building a factory to manufacture NAND flash memory chips in the United States, with upstate New York a leading candidate for the site, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The South Korean chipmaker faces growing pressure from the Trump administration to expand US manufacturing as Washington pushes to reshore semiconductor production and relentless investment in AI data centers has fuelled an acute shortage of memory chips.

The project would be separate from SK Hynix's discussions with Intel over manufacturing memory chips at Intel's Ohio facility, the sources said.

ตาก.title: โอลิค จัดเวทีแลกเปลี่ยน ‘รู้ก่อนเลือก’ วิธีคุมกำเนิด โรคติดต่อทางเพศสัมพันธ์ จนถึงการดูแลหลังพบ HPV
ตาก.summary:
OLIC จัดเวทีแลกเปลี่ยน ‘รู้ก่อนเลือก’ ยกระดับการสร้างความรอบรู้ด้านสุขภาพผู้หญิง
บริษัท โอลิค (ประเทศไทย) จำกัด (OLIC ) ในเครือ Fuji Pharma Group ประเทศญี่ปุ่น เดินหน้าสนับสนุนการสร้างความรอบรู้ด้านสุขภาพผู้หญิง (Women’s Health Literacy) ผ่านงาน “OLIC – Be with Her: Empowering Choices, World Contraception Day 2026” เปิดเวทีแลกเปลี่ยนความรู้ตั้งแต่การคุมกำเนิด การใช้ฮอร์โมนอย่างเหมาะสม การป้องกันโรคติดต่อทางเพศสัมพันธ์ ไปจนถึงการดูแลการติดเชื้อเอชพีวี (HPV) เมื่อวันที่ 16 กันยายนที่ผ่านมา ที่สำนักงานใหญ่ OLIC นิคมอุตสาหกรรมบางปะอิน จ.พระนครศรีอยุธยา
ภายในงาน เภสัชกรหญิงณัฐกานต์ ประสพสายพรกุล หรือเภสัชกรโน๊ต ร่วมสื่อสารประเด็นสุขภาพกับภาคีเครือข่ายด้านสุขภาพ เพื่อถ่ายทอดข้อมูลที่เข้าใจง่ายและนำไปใช้ได้จริง ภายใต้แนวคิด “Empowering Choices” OLIC เชื่อว่า “ทางเลือก” จะมีความหมายเมื่อผู้หญิงมีข้อมูลที่ถูกต้อง เข้าใจประโยชน์และความเสี่ยง และสามารถปรึกษาบุคลากรทางการแพทย์เพื่อเลือกแนวทางที่เหมาะสมกับตนเอง
นายทาเคฟุมิ ซากะระ (Mr. Takefumi Sagara) กรรมการผู้จัดการ บริษัท โอลิค (ประเทศไทย) จำกัด กล่าวว่า OLIC มองการส่งเสริมสุขภาพผู้หญิงอย่างรอบด้าน ตั้งแต่การป้องกัน การเข้าถึงข้อมูล การใช้ยาอย่างเหมาะสม ไปจนถึงการดูแลสุขภาพอย่างต่อเนื่อง “Our role is to be with her – not to make the decision for her, but to support her with knowledge, options and access to appropriate healthcare” สำหรับ OLIC การขับเคลื่อนสุขภาพผู้หญิง (Women’s Health) จึงให้ความสำคัญกับการสร้างความร่วมมือกับภาคีเครือข่ายด้านสุขภาพ เพื่อช่วยส่งต่อข้อมูลที่ถูกต้องและน่าเชื่อถือไปสู่ประชาชน

ทั้งนี้ หนึ่งในประเด็นที่ผู้เชี่ยวชาญให้ความสำคัญ คือการเปลี่ยนมุมมองต่อการเลือกยาคุมกำเนิด จากการพิจารณาเพียงประสิทธิภาพในการป้องกันการตั้งครรภ์ ไปสู่การพิจารณาประโยชน์ด้านสุขภาพอื่นๆ ควบคู่กับความปลอดภัยและความเหมาะสมของผู้หญิงแต่ละราย
รศ.ร.อ.นายแพทย์มานพชัย ธรรมคันโธ นายกสมาคมวางแผนครอบครัวแห่งประเทศไทยฯ กล่าวว่า ยาคุมกำเนิดอาจมีประโยชน์ด้านสุขภาพนอกเหนือจากการคุมกำเนิด เช่น ช่วยให้รอบเดือนสม่ำเสมอหรือลดอาการปวดประจำเดือน ขณะที่บางชนิดได้รับการขึ้นทะเบียนสำหรับข้อบ่งใช้เพิ่มเติม เช่น ภาวะปวดประจำเดือน (Dysmenorrhea) อย่างไรก็ตาม การเลือกใช้ควรพิจารณาประวัติสุขภาพ ปัจจัยเสี่ยง ชนิดของฮอร์โมน และเป้าหมายด้านสุขภาพของแต่ละบุคคล
นายแพทย์โอฬาริก มุสิกวงศ์ คณะทำงานรัฐมนตรีว่าการกระทรวงสาธารณสุข ด้านสื่อสารทางการแพทย์ เน้นว่า สำหรับผู้ที่ต้องใช้ฮอร์โมนในระยะยาว ควรให้ความสำคัญกับทั้งประสิทธิภาพ ความปลอดภัย และความเหมาะสมเฉพาะบุคคล ทั้งนี้ ยาคุมกำเนิดทุกชนิดมีข้อควรระวังและความเสี่ยงที่แตกต่างกัน ผู้หญิงควรปรึกษาแพทย์หรือเภสัชกร โดยเฉพาะเมื่อมีปัจจัยเสี่ยงหรือมีโรคประจำตัว
ปัจจุบันยาคุมกำเนิดชนิดฮอร์โมนรวม มีหลากหลายโมเลกุลของทั้ง Estrogen และ Progestin โดยหนึ่งในพัฒนาการของฮอร์โมนคุมกำเนิดคือ Estetrol (E4) ซึ่งเป็นเอสโตรเจนที่ร่างกายสร้างขึ้นตามธรรมชาติในช่วงพัฒนาการของทารกในครรภ์ และมีลักษณะการออกฤทธิ์ต่อเนื้อเยื่อที่แตกต่างจากเอสโตรเจนบางชนิดที่ใช้ในยาคุมกำเนิดแบบเดิม สะท้อนถึงแนวทางการพัฒนาทางเลือกด้านการคุมกำเนิดที่หลากหลายขึ้น ทั้งนี้การเลือกใช้ควรคำนึงถึงข้อควรระวังและความเหมาะสมของผู้หญิงแต่ละราย
ขณะที่เภสัชกรหญิงชนากิตต์ อิ่มบำรุง เหรัญญิก สภาเภสัชกรรม กล่าวว่า เภสัชกรชุมชน มีบทบาทสำคัญในการช่วยผู้หญิงประเมินความเหมาะสมก่อนเลือกใช้ยา โดยเฉพาะในยุคที่ข้อมูลจากรีวิวและสื่อออนไลน์มีอิทธิพลต่อการตัดสินใจ
“บทบาทของเภสัชกรชุมชน ไม่ใช่เพียงการจ่ายยา แต่คือการช่วยถามให้ครบ ประเมินให้เหมาะ และแนะนำให้ถูกต้อง ทั้งประวัติสุขภาพ ปัจจัยเสี่ยง ยาที่ใช้อยู่ และสัญญาณเตือนที่ควรส่งต่อแพทย์”
ทั้งนี้ การสร้าง Health Literacy จึงไม่ใช่เพียงการให้ข้อมูล แต่คือการช่วยให้ผู้หญิง “รู้ว่าอะไรควรถาม รู้ว่าต้องประเมินอะไร และรู้ว่าเมื่อใดควรพบแพทย์” เพื่อให้การตัดสินใจด้านสุขภาพเกิดขึ้นบนพื้นฐานของข้อมูลที่ถูกต้อง…
ตาก.source: มติชนออนไลน์

ตาก.title: Chonburi Hospital explains controversy over locked disabled patient’s car
ตาก.summary:
CHONBURI — 17 September 2026, Chonburi Hospital has clarified a widely shared incident involving a man whose car was wheel-locked after he parked in a disabled parking space while picking up his father, who has a leg disability, from the hospital.
The incident sparked criticism online after a video showed the man’s vehicle being wheel-locked by a security guard.
In a statement issued on Thursday, Chonburi Hospital said the parking area where the incident occurred does not belong to the hospital.
The hospital said the area is a parking facility operated by a private hospital foundation. The foundation’s chairman and board members are not currently hospital employees, and the hospital has no role in managing the privately owned area.
The hospital also explained that it has designated disabled parking spaces of its own in front of the hospital entrance.

Security personnel are assigned to those spaces to provide assistance and facilitate access for patients with disabilities, according to the statement.
Although the incident did not take place on hospital property, Chonburi Hospital said it had contacted the foundation that owns the parking area following the incident.
The hospital said it would work with the foundation to discuss the incident, clarify the circumstances and seek measures to prevent similar situations from happening again.
Chonburi Hospital reaffirmed its commitment to providing healthcare services with attention to the needs of all patients, including people with disabilities, and to facilitating access to its services.

ตาก.title: From ‘Grey Jews’ to Perceived Zionist Neo-Occupation Threats in Thailand
ตาก.summary:
In an interview with an Israeli media outlet published earlier this week, Israeli Ambassador to Thailand Alona Fisher-Kamm acknowledged that anti-Israel sentiment in Thailand had shifted from anger among some Thais over rude Israeli tourists, law-breaking tourists and expats to people chanting “Free Palestine” outside the embassy.
In an interview with Ynetnews, an Israeli news website, the article noted that Fisher-Kamm said the protest outside the embassy “also demonstrated that the issue had begun to extend beyond tourism.”
Ynetnews then quoted the ambassador:
“If the demonstration had only been about improving Israeli behavior or opposing the presence of Israelis in Thailand, then chants of ‘Free Palestine’ and insults against Jews should not have been there.”
Indeed, there are different players in this fluid and rapidly evolving development. So here are some key players and groups worth noticing.
Te Acheewa’s “Thai Intolerance” group
Te was previously known for his video-recorded raid on illegal migrant workers and had established himself as an ultra-royalist before taking up the anti-“Grey Jews” crusade. He staged the first anti-grey-Israeli demonstration outside the Israeli Embassy in Bangkok, a week before the Sondhi Limthongkul-led demonstration at the same site.
He also led some 500 or so demonstrators outside a Chabad House in Patong, Phuket, last week, which eventually led to the cancellation of the Jewish New Year celebrations there after the Chabad House announced that it had been advised by Israeli security authorities not to go ahead with the celebrations.
Although Te originally said his group had nothing to do with what’s happening in Gaza, the occupied West Bank and beyond, but was strictly about Thai affairs, the man, who has a million followers on Facebook, claims that he is now being monitored by Mossad, Israel’s secret service.
He posted the following message (in Thai) earlier this week:
“A message to you, Mossad and your lot:
If you think I’m afraid of you, I wouldn’t be stepping forward to defend Thai people in the first place.
“And most importantly, I fight with the truth and what is right. If you and your followers are unhappy with me, I challenge you right here: come and face me directly. Don’t attack me from behind like a coward. That’s pathetic.
“You are born once and you die once. But what I do will be remembered for a long time, because I “fight for Thai people”. I will never bow my head to you, you fucking bastard, Mossad.
“#TeAcheewa #ThailandWillNotTolerateThis #ThisIsThailand”
On the group’s Facebook page, which has more than 100,000 members, a member shared lessons drawn from what he says is happening in Cyprus.
Here is Najm Murshid’s post (from Thai) to the group from Tuesday night:
“I would suggest that those who act as cheerleaders for Israel, or those who make a living from and benefit economically from Israel, come together and collect signatures calling for Israeli communities to be established in areas near their own homes — including Chabad centres, cemeteries, and the purchase of houses and land in their neighbourhoods.
“Don’t just cheer for or defend Israelis taking over economic areas. Israelis tend to choose beautiful, prime tourist locations when they settle or do business. In Thailand, places such as Pai, Phangan, Samui and Phuket are beautiful and commercially valuable. ตาก.title: Chonburi Hospital explains controversy over locked disabled patient’s car
ตาก.summary:
CHONBURI — 17 September 2026, Chonburi Hospital has clarified a widely shared incident involving a man whose car was wheel-locked after he parked in a disabled parking space while picking up his father, who has a leg disability, from the hospital.
The incident sparked criticism online after a video showed the man’s vehicle being wheel-locked by a security guard.
In a statement issued on Thursday, Chonburi Hospital said the parking area where the incident occurred does not belong to the hospital.
The hospital said the area is a parking facility operated by a private hospital foundation. The foundation’s chairman and board members are not currently hospital employees, and the hospital has no role in managing the privately owned area.
The hospital also explained that it has designated disabled parking spaces of its own in front of the hospital entrance.

Security personnel are assigned to those spaces to provide assistance and facilitate access for patients with disabilities, according to the statement.
Although the incident did not take place on hospital property, Chonburi Hospital said it had contacted the foundation that owns the parking area following the incident.
The hospital said it would work with the foundation to discuss the incident, clarify the circumstances and seek measures to prevent similar situations from happening again.
Chonburi Hospital reaffirmed its commitment to providing healthcare services with attention to the needs of all patients, including people with disabilities, and to facilitating access to its services.

ตาก.title: Anutin Orders Rules to Stop Foreign Data Center Abuse
ตาก.summary:
BANGKOK – Thailand is taking a firm stand against foreign data center operators who try to bend the rules. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul recently chaired the first meeting of the newly formed National Data Center Policy Committee. He made it very clear that the country welcomes investment, but not at the cost of its citizens or environment. The rapid growth of the industry requires strict new rules to prevent exploitation.

The prime minister stated that data center regulations cannot simply suit everyone’s wishes. He ordered immediate measures to stop operators from breaking Thai laws or taking advantage of the local system. The government is now moving fast to create a clear legal framework. This will quickly close the loopholes that some companies have used to avoid proper regulatory oversight.

For a long time, data centers operated in a gray area without direct laws controlling them. Some foreign operators took advantage of this lack of regulation to easily lower their costs. They registered their large tech facilities simply as standard warehouses. This sneaky move allowed them to skip mandatory Environmental Impact Assessments entirely. Because of this, surrounding neighborhoods suffered from noise, pollution, and unregulated fuel storage.

Prime Minister Anutin praised local officials for inspecting these sites and finding these hidden operations. He warned that this kind of secret behavior must stop immediately for the public good. Authorities will now clearly define what a data center actually is under Thai law. They will also set minimum safety and environmental standards for every specific area.

The government wants to ensure that these massive facilities do not harm local communities. If companies want to build in Thailand, they must strictly follow proper zoning laws and building codes. City officials will review these plans carefully before giving out any new permits. According to a recent report, the state is fully prepared to enact dedicated laws to maintain strict oversight.

Data centers use a massive amount of water and electricity to keep their servers cool. Recently, power requests from these operators surged to nearly 20,000 megawatts. This huge number is almost equal to the entire electricity demand of the whole country. Prime Minister Anutin noted that many of these massive requests were actually speculative and unfair.

Some companies were trying to reserve large amounts of power just to resell it later. The government will now tighten the rules to end this greedy practice completely. Power allotments will no longer be allowed to expire unused or be traded commercially. Instead, the electricity must be used fairly and efficiently for real tech projects.

To protect the environment, the prime minister is also pushing for stricter clean energy standards. Operators will be required to use renewable sources like wind and solar power. This move directly aligns with Thailand’s goal to reach net-zero carbon emissions in the future. The government wants the digital economy to grow sustainably without relying heavily on dirty fossil fuels.

Thailand wants more than just large buildings filled with blinking computer servers. Prime Minister Anutin stressed that these investments must create real added value for the nation. The country expects foreign operators to help develop the local workforce and share important technology. Thailand aims to become a true digital hub, not just a cheap dumping ground for servers.

ตาก.title: Chiang Rai Trains 60 Volunteers to Cut Farm Burning
ตาก.summary:
Chiang Rai has taken a bold step to clear its skies and improve public health. The province recently deployed 60 energy volunteers across 18 different districts to tackle farm burning. These dedicated locals are actively teaching rural communities how to use innovative biochar technology. This smart approach turns leftover crop waste into a valuable resource instead of harmful smoke.

For years, open field burning after harvest has choked Northern Thailand with thick smog. Farmers often burn corn stalks and rice straw to clear land quickly and cheaply. However, this practice releases massive amounts of dangerous PM2.5 pollution into the air we breathe. By introducing biochar, officials hope to give farmers a cleaner, more profitable alternative to lighting matches.

Breathing clean air is a basic human right, yet seasonal smog heavily impacts the region. The tiny PM2.5 particles easily enter the lungs, causing severe long-term respiratory health issues. Local tourism and the regional economy also suffer greatly when the skies turn hazy. This new volunteer initiative is a direct, practical response to these ongoing environmental challenges.

Instead of setting fields on fire, farmers are learning a new method called pyrolysis. This process involves baking organic waste at high temperatures with very little oxygen. The result is biochar, a stable, charcoal-like substance that safely locks away carbon. Making biochar stops harmful smoke from entering the atmosphere and choking local villages.

These 60 trained energy volunteers act as community coaches in their respective home districts. They provide hands-on training to show neighbors exactly how to build and use simple biochar kilns. These kilns can process everyday agricultural leftovers like corn cobs, stalks, roots, and husks. By sharing this practical knowledge locally, the volunteers make the transition away from burning much easier.

The benefits of biochar extend far beyond just cleaning up the air we breathe. When mixed into the earth, biochar acts like a sponge to hold vital water and nutrients. This improves soil health dramatically, meaning farmers can spend less money on expensive chemical fertilizers. It is a practical solution that saves money while protecting the local environment at the same time.

Local companies are also getting involved to support this important green agricultural shift. Recent private projects in areas like the Wiang Pa Pao district have started processing local crop by-products. This industrial scale effort turns massive amounts of agricultural waste into verifiable carbon storage. Such partnerships show that reducing pollution can actually create exciting new green business opportunities.

Furthermore, using biochar helps fight global climate change by storing carbon safely in the ground. Plants naturally pull carbon dioxide from the air as they grow in the fields. Normally, rotting or burning these plants releases that carbon right back into the sky. Biochar traps this carbon safely in the soil for hundreds of years, making agriculture much greener.

ตาก.title: Thailand pushes creative economy to become a Creative Nation
ตาก.summary:
Thailand is looking to its creative economy as a new engine of growth, with the Creative Economy Agency (CEA) seeking to turn local culture, talent and city identities into economic opportunities and attract visitors and investment from around the world.
CEA says the country’s creative economy is currently worth about 1.7 trillion baht, equivalent to 10.8% of Thailand’s gross value added (GVA), with nearly 1 million people working in creative industries.
The World Bank’s Building Thailand’s Future Today (2026) report has identified creative industries as one of five sectors with strong potential to drive future productivity, investment and quality employment in Thailand.

CEA says developing the sector requires simultaneous investment in people, businesses and cities , allowing local communities to build on their existing cultural and creative assets.
Local food, crafts, culture, design and creative talent can be developed into products, services, experiences and content that reflect the identity of individual cities, while festivals and other creative activities can help connect those identities with tourism and investment opportunities.
Festivals become platforms for local growth
One of CEA’s key tools is the development of creative festivals as platforms for local economic activity.
Its Festival Creator 2026 programme, now in its second year, aims to strengthen the skills of local festival organisers and encourage events that reflect the identity of their communities.
The programme focuses on three levels: developing people with professional event-management skills; helping festivals establish distinctive identities; and using festivals to generate jobs, income and new recognition for their host cities.

Six festivals in five provinces are receiving support this year: Kenduri Seni Tolong Menolong 2026 in Pattani; TAK: A Taste of Roots in Tak; Pakad Art Awakening Market Vol. 2 in Chiang Rai; Hug HeartYai and Singorama Art Fest 2026 in Songkhla; and Taiban Land Camp in Sisaket.
CEA says the festivals provide platforms for local people to showcase their skills, build networks, experiment with new ideas and create business opportunities.
The approach is part of CEA’s wider concept of turning cities into a “City as a Stage” , where artists, designers, entrepreneurs and communities can work together to create new economic and cultural value.
Building city brands from local identity
CEA is also working on city branding through its Neramyth City: Branding Cities into Creative Assets project, in cooperation with the Tourism Authority of Thailand and nine model cities: Phetchaburi, Sakon Nakhon, Nakhon Si Thammarat, Pattani, Ratchaburi, Lamphun, Sisaket, Sing Buri and Ubon Ratchathani.
The agency says city branding is not simply about creating a logo, slogan or mascot. Instead, it involves identifying the “DNA” of a city through collaboration between government, businesses, communities, artists, creative professionals and residents.

The project involves three main stages: developing a city brand strategy, testing the brand through real-world activities and experiences, and developing the city’s brand identity.
The resulting identities include “Ubon the Beautiful Paradox” for Ubon Ratchathani, “Sappaya Sakon: The Beauty of the Ordinary” for Sakon Nakhon and “Phetchaburi: City of Origins” for Phetchaburi.

ตาก.title: Malaysia’s king allows former leader Najib to serve rest of his graft sentence under house arrest
ตาก.summary:
KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia (AP) — Malaysia’s king on Friday granted jailed former Prime Minister Najib Razak a rare royal clemency, allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison term for graft under house arrest.
The decision came at a suddenly convened Pardons Board meeting, a week after the board deferred Najib’s latest clemency application to a future meeting. It marked an unprecedented use of house arrest as a form of royal clemency in Malaysia and could renew debate over royal powers, the rule of law and the treatment of Malaysia’s most prominent corruption convict.
A statement issued by the Legal Affairs Department under the Prime Minister’s office said Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar has granted a “conditional pardon” for Najib during a Pardons Board meeting. Najib will be allowed to serve the remainder of his prison term under house arrest until Aug. 23, 2028, if he pays the 50 million ringgit fine ($12 million) imposed by the court, it said.
The statement said Najib must also follow conditions set, failing which the pardon will be forfeited. No details were provided.
Najib, 73, has been imprisoned since August 2022 after Malaysia’s top court upheld his conviction in a graft case linked to the multi-billion dollar looting of the state investment fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad.
He was originally sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined 210 million ringgit ($51.5 million) in 2020 for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving 42 million ringgit ($10.3 million) channeled into his bank accounts from SRC International, a former unit of 1MDB.
In January 2024, a Pardons Board chaired by the then-king halved his sentence to six years and reduced his fine to 50 million ringgit.
Najib has maintained the previous king, Sultan Abdullah Ahmad Shah, also issued an addendum order allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. But the High Court ruled that the alleged house arrest order was not enforceable because it had not been raised or discussed by the Pardons Board at its January 2024 meeting.
The house-arrest order also raises questions about a separate graft sentence for Najib.
In December 2025, Najib was found guilty for abuse of power and money laundering related to over $700 million channeled into his bank accounts from 1MDB, in his main trial tied to the fund. He was sentenced to another 15 years in prison and fined 11.4 billion ringgit ($2.8 billion), which is to take effect after his existing sentence ends. He is appealing that conviction.
House arrest had been discussed as part of broader criminal-justice reforms in Malaysia. In 2024, the government said proposed legislation allowing home detention in certain circumstances was aimed at reducing prison overcrowding and recidivism, not designed specifically for Najib.
Najib set up the 1MDB development fund shortly after he took office in 2009. Investigators allege at least $4.5 billion was stolen from the fund and laundered by Najib’s associates through layers of bank accounts in the U.S. and other countries. The funds were allegedly used to finance Hollywood films and extravagant purchases that included hotels, a luxury yacht, art and jewelry.
A national outrage over the 1MDB scandal led to the historic 2018 election defeat of the party that had governed Malaysia since independence from Britain in 1957.

ตาก.title: Indonesia welcomes its first aircraft carrier, prompting debate over cost and military ambitions
ตาก.summary:
JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Indonesia welcomed its first aircraft carrier Friday, a former Italian warship that the government says will strengthen the archipelago nation’s maritime security and disaster response capabilities.
The 41-year-old former ITS Giuseppe Garibaldi, with capacity for short takeoff and vertical landing aircraft and helicopters, was welcomed with a military ceremony upon its arrival at a naval base in North Jakarta’s Tanjung Priok seaport.
Italy in March agreed to give the carrier, which was retired in 2024, to Indonesia in a move aimed at boosting Italy’s broader defense engagement with the Southeast Asian country. Italy is seeking deals on submarines and aircraft, and gifting the carrier to Indonesia also saves it the cost of decommissioning the ship.
“We intend to use the ship primarily for military operations other than war, although it can also be deployed for combat missions if necessary,” Indonesian Navy chief Adm. Muhammad Ali told reporters after the ceremony. He said the carrier could serve the navy for another 15 to 20 years and could accommodate 14 helicopters or more, depending on their size.
Indonesia will become the second country in Southeast Asia with an aircraft carrier. Thailand’s HTMS Chakri Naruebet was commissioned in 1997 after being procured from Spain along with carrier-capable AV-8S Matador jump jets.
Ali said the carrier will be commissioned into the navy next week as the KRI Sriwijaya, honoring the Srivijaya empire, a maritime kingdom based in Sumatra that became one of Southeast Asia’s dominant naval and trading powers between the seventh and 13th centuries. Previously, the navy would name the carrier as KRI Gajah Mada.
Defense development was one of the top priorities for President Prabowo Subianto’s administration, as he has advocated an expansion of the military through the purchase of submarines, frigates, fighter jets , and missiles and pushed for more defense cooperation with various countries.
Indonesian Navy personnel and crew members stand aboard the Giuseppe Garibaldi, a former Italian Navy aircraft carrier, after its arrival at Tanjung Priok port in Jakarta, Indonesia, Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Tatan Syuflana)
But the Garibaldi acquisition has raised questions about whether Indonesia needs an aircraft carrier at all and whether the government should be spending millions of dollars to refurbish and operate an aging warship.
Indonesia’s Finance Ministry approved $450 million in financing for the aircraft carrier program in 2025. However, some lawmakers have warned the overall bill could be far higher. TB Hasanuddin, a member of Parliament’s Commission I, said the cost of retrofitting the carrier alone could reach 16 trillion rupiah (about $900 million).
Indonesia to convert the Garibaldi for handling disasters
Unlike major naval powers that use aircraft carriers to launch fighter jets far from home shores, Indonesia views the vessel as a mobile command center and support hub for helicopters, uncrewed aircraft and maritime operations across its thousands of islands.
Speaking during a disaster management meeting early this month, Prabowo said the vessel would help authorities combat forest and peatland fires that regularly blanket parts of Southeast Asia with hazardous haze.
“We will refurbish it and convert it into a carrier for helicopters and drones,” Prabowo said in a video briefing. “This will greatly help our disaster response.”

ตาก.title: Heavy rain and floods in northern Vietnam submerge homes and disrupt economy
ตาก.summary:
HANOI, Vietnam (AP) — Heavy rain caused flooding across parts of northern Vietnam on Thursday, disrupting travel, inundating homes and pushing several rivers above dangerous levels, authorities and state media said.
Rain has fallen across northern and north-central Vietnam this week, with some areas receiving more than 50 centimeters (19.7 inches), according to the disaster prevention department.
More than 2,000 homes have been submerged, many key transportation routes blocked and more than 1,000 households isolated. Ninh Binh and Thanh Hoa provinces, which include lowland and hilly areas south of the capital Hanoi, have been among the hardest hit.
Vietnam is among the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries and prone to flooding. A series of severe storms last year spurred the country to find new ways to prepare for and manage floods .
Local residents commute by boat through a flooded village on the outskirts of Hanoi, Vietnam Thursday, Sep. 17, 2026. (Pham Tuan Anh/VNA via AP)
In Thanh Hoa province, authorities told students to stay home because flooding had made travel to school dangerous, state media said.
Heavy rains and flooding have submerged or damaged about 10,014 hectares (24,745 acres) of rice and other crops, with the largest losses reported in Ninh Binh, Thanh Hoa and Nghe An provinces. Thousands of livestock and poultry also have been killed.
“The flood happens every year,” Ninh Binh resident Tran Ngoc Tai told national broadcaster VTV, adding that people were prepared with fresh water and food.
Many streets in Hanoi were deeply flooded Thursday morning, with water nearly a meter (3.2 feet) deep in some places, disrupting traffic and making it difficult for residents to get to work, take children to school or leave their homes.
Rainfall from Wednesday night to Thursday morning exceeded 15 centimeters (5.9 inches) in some areas, state media said.
Many high schools and universities in Hanoi remained closed or switched to online classes Thursday afternoon as heavy rain caused widespread flooding.
The rising waters of Bui River in the southwest outskirts of Hanoi threatened to flood homes, prompting authorities to deploy hundreds of soldiers to help residents move belongings to higher ground, state media said.
Local residents commute by boat through a flooded village on the outskirts of Hanoi, Vietnam Thursday, Sep. 17, 2026. (Nhat Anh/VNA via AP)
A cold air mass moving south is expected to bring five days of heavy rain to southern Vietnam including flood-prone Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam’s financial capital, starting Sept. 17, according to the Southern Regional Hydro-Meteorological Center.
Forecasters predict widespread rain through Sept. 21. Authorities have warned of flooding in low-lying areas and along waterways. Ho Chi Minh City is forecast to receive 10 to 20 centimeters (4 to 8 inches) of rain, with some areas getting more.
Vietnam experienced repeated severe flooding in 2025. Tropical Storm Wipha brought heavy rain and flooding in July, followed by more flooding and landslides in August when Tropical Storm Kajiki struck. Typhoon Bualoi killed at least 26 in September. In October, the historic cities of Hue and Hoi An in central Vietnam flooded, along with much of northern Vietnam .

ตาก.title: Chud Thai takes centre stage at Tokyo National Museum
ตาก.summary:
Thailand’s Ministry of Culture has showcased the knowledge, craftsmanship and traditions behind Chud Thai at the Tokyo National Museum in Japan, presenting the traditional dress as a living cultural heritage that can continue to evolve.
The “CHUD THAI: Knowledge, Craftsmanship and Practices of the Thai National Costume” event was held on 17–18 September at the Hyokeikan building of the Tokyo National Museum in Tokyo.

The programme featured discussions by Assistant Professor Dr Anucha Teerakanont, director of the Institute for the Promotion of Thai Arts, and Piyawara Teekara Netnoy, director of the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles.
An exhibition presented all eight styles of Chud Thai known as the “royal” Thai dresses, designed and tailored by Tirapan and Pha fashion houses.
The exhibition also featured a kimono worn by Her Royal Highness Princess Sirivannavari Nariratana Rajakanya, made from mudmee silk produced under the SUPPORT Foundation.
Visitors could also see demonstrations of traditional Thai craftsmanship, including ancient jewellery making, gold-thread wrapping and embroidery, silver and gold craftsmanship, traditional gold-leaf textile techniques and auspicious-pattern silk weaving.

The organisers presented these crafts as contemporary forms of design rooted in artistic structures, rather than simply historical objects, highlighting Thai craftsmanship as living heritage that can be developed further.
One of the highlights was a Ruean Ton-style Chud Thai from Montratikarn Studio, one of the eight royal Chud Thai styles. The dress was modelled by Opal Suchata Chuangsri.
The pale-yellow outfit featured a sarong decorated with hand-embroidered Sailor Moon motifs across the fabric rather than printed designs, combining Thai and Japanese cultural elements.

The fashion house also prepared textiles featuring Hello Kitty and Shiba Inu patterns, incorporating symbols associated with Japanese culture into the exhibition.

ตาก.title: 7,898 apply for Thai military volunteer programme in 8 days
ตาก.summary:
Thailand’s Defence Ministry said 7,898 people had applied to join the “Volunteer Soldier” programme for the 2027 intake during its first eight days, reaching 31.59% of the 25,000 positions available.
The ministry released the figures on 18 September, covering applications submitted between 10 and 17 September.
A total of 492 people applied on 17 September alone, including 427 for the Royal Thai Army, 37 for the Royal Thai Navy, 24 for the Royal Thai Air Force and four for the Royal Thai Armed Forces Headquarters.
Of the 7,898 applicants, 5,391 were conscripts, 1,309 were Category 1 reserve soldiers and 1,198 were serving soldiers whose discharge dates had been extended.
The Defence Ministry said the figures from the first eight days reflected not only interest in military service but also the programme’s aim of giving young people more options to make decisions and plan their futures.
The Volunteer Soldier programme is designed to turn military service into an opportunity through benefits and welfare, personal development, education, career development and preparation for the future.
“When volunteer soldiers join, we must give them opportunities in return,” the ministry said.
Applications for the 2027 programme opened on 10 September and will remain open until 24 January 2027 through an online system. The first selection is scheduled for 28 November 2026.
ตาก.title_original: 7,898 apply for Thai military volunteer programme in 8 days
ตาก.summary_original:
Thailand’s Defence Ministry said 7,898 people had applied to join the “Volunteer Soldier” programme for the 2027 intake during its first eight days, reaching 31.59% of the 25,000 positions available.

The ministry released the figures on 18 September, covering applications submitted between 10 and 17 September.

A total of 492 people applied on 17 September alone, including 427 for the Royal Thai Army, 37 for the Royal Thai Navy, 24 for the Royal Thai Air Force and four for the Royal Thai Armed Forces Headquarters.

Of the 7,898 applicants, 5,391 were conscripts, 1,309 were Category 1 reserve soldiers and 1,198 were serving soldiers whose discharge dates had been extended.

The Defence Ministry said the figures from the first eight days reflected not only interest in military service but also the programme’s aim of giving young people more options to make decisions and plan their futures.

The Volunteer Soldier programme is designed to turn military service into an opportunity through benefits and welfare, personal development, education, career development and preparation for the future.

“When volunteer soldiers join, we must give them opportunities in return,” the ministry said.

Applications for the 2027 programme opened on 10 September and will remain open until 24 January 2027 through an online system. The first selection is scheduled for 28 November 2026.

ตาก.title: Australian man pleads not guilty to Thai suitcase murder
ตาก.summary:
The man had been charged with murder, concealing a body and taking a minor for indecent purposes.

BANGKOK: An Australian accused of murdering a Thai teenager and stuffing her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday (Sep 18) in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said.

Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested at a Bangkok airport on Jun 26 as he prepared to take a flight back to Australia, after the 17-year-old victim's friend reported her missing.

Her body was found in a suitcase near a railway track in Pattaya, a city south of Bangkok, early the next day.

Carman appeared on Friday at Pattaya Provincial Court, where he pleaded not guilty to all charges, a court spokesperson told AFP.

He had been charged with murder, concealing a body and taking a minor for indecent purposes. The next court date was set for Oct 12.

Police previously said CCTV footage showed him entering a condominium in Pattaya with the girl in the early hours of Jun 25, and leaving that evening carrying a large black suitcase.

The case put the spotlight on Pattaya, which is popular with foreign tourists for its beaches and nightlife, but also has a reputation for sex tourism.
